name: Tina Smith
stance: Says AI companies cannot regulate themselves and should be prosecuted and held liable when their models cause harm, wanted a mutual AI slowdown agreement with China, and criticizes stalled Senate AI safety talks.

statements.text: These big AI companies should be held civilly and/or criminally liable and prosecuted when their models hurt people. They don’t get a free pass just because they’ve now decided to admit to the dangers of what they’ve created.
While he’s blocked any effort to rein in AI in Congress, that doesn’t mean there aren’t laws on the books we can use to protect people right now.
These AI companies cannot be trusted to regulate themselves. Don’t let the fox guard the henhouse.
AI developers aren’t above the laws we have currently on the books. They can and should be prosecuted and held liable if they break the law and their products harm us.
Trusting the same DOJ that covered up the Epstein Files to protect us from frontier AI… What could possibly go wrong?
We needed a comprehensive agreement with China to a mutual slowdown of AI development. Instead, we get nothing.
You’re telling me the guy who said “LET DATA REIGN” just poured cold water on the only bipartisan AI safety talks that seem promising?
AI companies love to claim they’re SO special they need special treatment and can’t follow the same rules other dangerous technologies are bound by
So, apparently AI can now literally try to take your money straight from the bank. Remind me again why letting Big Tech regulate itself could ever be a good idea?
Congress needs to get serious about holding Big Tech accountable and creating AI guardrails. Now.
